To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel immunoblotting method for the diagnosis of Hermanssky-Pudlak syndrome and have used it to determine that BLOC-2 and BLOC-3 are the protein complexes that are defective in two new HPS patients.
the molecular diagnosis of HPS can be facilitated by an immunoblotting approach that allows the identification of the defective complex and, in some cases, the identification of the mutated gene.

we have developed a simple and reliable biochemical method to determine the HPS type, which has allowed us to identify two novel mutations and to estimate the native molecular mass (140+/-30kDa) of BLOC-1, a previously undescribed complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a biochemical assay that will facilitate molecular diagnosis of HPS and other disorders involving lysosome-related organelles.
the identification and characterization of new HPS subunits, which may help in the diagnosis of HPS.

the development of a molecular diagnosis assay for HPS, which should facilitate the molecular diagnosis in HPS patients of different ethnic origin and should help to elucidate the structure of BLOC-1 and BLOC-3.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BLOC-1, -2 and -3 are heterodimers composed of two subunits each, whereas the AP-3 complex is a heterotetramer.
BLOC-1, -2, and -3 are heterotrimers, AP-3 is a heteropentamer, and HPS1 and HPS4 constitute a heterodimer.
the biochemical analysis of HPS patients has allowed us to define the HPS complex affected and, in the case of BLOC-1 and -3, the specific mutated subunits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the assay is an excellent tool for facilitating the molecular diagnosis of HPS.
the immunoblotting-based assay can be used to facilitate the molecular analysis of patients with unknown genetic defects, and that the BLOC-3 complex is most likely a heterodimer.
the biochemical approach described here can be used as a diagnostic tool for HPS patients and that BLOC-2, BLOC-3, and AP-3 are all heteromeric protein complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
immunoblotting can be an important component in the molecular diagnosis of HPS.
the immunoblotting method can be applied to any protein complex, and can facilitate the molecular diagnosis and genetic counselling of patients with a wide variety of diseases.

the immunoblotting method described here will allow the molecular diagnosis of HPS in most patients to be based on the analysis of a small subset of the candidate genes, thus greatly reducing the time and cost of diagnosis.
